name: bluewater-20-can-you-keep-all-three
lines: You have three customers. By five o'clock, you'll probably have one.
This is a game. You make the calls. I tell you what it cost you.
Keep score. Three customers. Four decisions. Go.
It's Monday. Seven a.m. You're a handyman now. Congratulations. Your back already hurts.
Customer one. Dot. Eighty one. A regular. She brings you banana bread.
Customer two. Brent. Brand new. Wants a whole bathroom redone. Big job.
Customer three. Kim. She manages twelve rental units. That could be twelve years of work.
They're all made up. The decisions aren't.
Decision one.
Seven fifteen. You're driving. Dot calls. At the same second, Brent emails, asking for a quote.
A. Answer Dot. Or B. Pull over and email Brent, because he's the money.
Choose. Three. Two. One.
If you picked B. Dot was calling to book you. She gets voicemail. She calls her son. Her son knows a guy. You will never taste that banana bread again.
If you picked A. Smart. Dot takes ninety seconds. Brent's email can wait an hour. Emails don't hang up.
Rule one. A ringing phone beats a typed message. Every time.
Decision two.
Ten a.m. You're on a ladder at Dot's. Brent calls. You have four screws in your mouth.
A. Let it go to voicemail, and call back at lunch. Or B. Send a ten second text. On a ladder. Call you at twelve.
Choose. Three. Two. One.
If you picked A. By lunch, Brent has called two other guys. One picked up. You're now competing for a job that was yours at ten a.m.
If you picked B. Brent reads it and thinks, this one's organized. He waits. People wait when they know how long.
Rule two. Silence feels like no. A time feels like yes.
Decision three.
Noon. You call Brent. He wants a price for the bathroom. Right now. On the phone.
A. Throw out a number so you don't lose him. Or B. Say, I'll come see it tomorrow at eight, and you'll have it in writing by dinner.
Choose. Three. Two. One.
If you picked A. Say you blurted eight thousand. It's a twelve thousand dollar bathroom. Now you're either losing money, or you're the guy who raised his price.
If you picked B. He's a little annoyed. For about a day. Then the quote shows up exactly when you said. And annoyed turns into impressed.
Rule three. A fast guess costs more than a slow answer.
Decision four. The hard one.
Three p.m. Kim calls. The front door in unit seven won't lock. A tenant with a newborn. She needs someone today.
But you promised Dot you'd be back at four to finish her gate.
A. Go to Kim. It's twelve units. Dot will understand. Or B. Keep your word to Dot, and tell Kim you can't.
Choose. Three. Two. One.
Trick question. They're both wrong.
Pick A, and you broke a promise to the customer who's been with you nine years. Dot does understand. Dot also tells her entire bridge club.
Pick B, and you just told a property manager with twelve units, no. She has a list. You're not on it anymore.
The answer was C. Pick up the phone. Twice.
Call Dot. I've got an emergency. A baby, and a door that won't lock. Can I finish your gate at eight tomorrow? I'll bring the banana bread this time.
Dot says, go. Of course she does. You asked.
Then call Kim. I'll be there by four.
Rule four. Most customers can handle a change of plans. Nobody can handle finding out on their own.
Final score.
Kept all three? You're running a real business. Also, you cheated. I saw you change your answer on number four.
Kept two? That's a normal Monday.
One, or zero? Relax. You've been a handyman for four minutes. Real ones get to practice.
Here's what the game was really about.
Not one of those decisions was about tools.
The phone. The text. The quote. The promise.
That's the whole job nobody trains you for.
The honest part. Real days are messier. Sometimes you do everything right, and Brent still hires his brother in law.
No rule wins every customer.
But these four cost nothing.
Answer the ring. Send the time. Quote it in writing. Call before they find out.
Comment your score. And be honest. Dot is watching.
If you want your marketing handled while you're up the ladder, that's what we do. Bluewater Co dot C A.
